lesson.grammar_point: used to / didn't use to / did you use to (past habits and states)

vocab.title: Match each word to its meaning
defs: Not common: it does not happen very often
All the forms and documents you have to fill in
At the present time, compared with the past
How long a person has to wait for something
To put something new in the place of something old
Normal: it happens often, or there are many of it
The machines and tools you need for a job

items.situation: Tell me one thing your job used to be like twenty years ago.
Ask me about my first job, with used to.
Say one thing you didn't use to do, but you do nowadays.
tips: I didn't use to..., but nowadays I...

items.situation: A partner asks: Was CAR-T common in Brazil ten years ago? Answer.
tips: No, it used to be rare.

items.situation: Tell me one thing in your hospital that computers or tablets replaced.
Tell me what you miss from your first years at work.

listenings.text: My name is Roberto, and I have been a nurse in oncology for thirty years. When I started, things were very different. We used to write everything on paper, and the paperwork used to take about two hours every day. Patients used to come from very far away, and many of them used to stay in the city for months. Nowadays, a lot of them do their treatment at a partner hospital near their home. The equipment is different too. The machines used to be huge and very slow. Now they are smaller and much faster. But one thing did not change. The patient still needs a person who listens. That part of my job is the same as thirty years ago.

When I was younger, I used to travel all the time. I used to visit three or four hospitals every month, in different countries. Honestly, I didn't use to have a home life. My suitcase was always open. Then the pandemic came, and everything changed. Nowadays, most of my meetings are video calls, and I travel only twice a year. Some people think video calls are worse, but I am not sure. I used to spend two days on a trip for a one-hour meeting. Now I spend those two days with my clients' numbers, and my advice is better. I still love visiting hospitals, like this trip to Sao Paulo. But now a visit is rare, so it is special.
